candidate.blueprint_topic: Prevention of cross-contamination during shared pulmonary-function testing
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent cross-contamination during shared spirometry by changing the patient-contact mouthpiece and filter between clients.

options.A: Change the spirometer mouthpiece and filter before the next client uses the equipment
options.B: Keep the same mouthpiece in place if it appears visibly clean
options.C: Replace the mouthpiece only at the end of the testing day
options.D: Reuse the same mouthpiece after wiping only its outside surface

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current CDC disinfection guidance notes that mouthpieces and spirometry tubing can become contaminated with microorganisms and that, when filters are used to protect equipment distal to the filter, the filter and proximal mouthpiece are changed between patients. CDC's pneumonia-prevention guidance likewise directs changing the mouthpiece and filter of a spirometer between different patients. B, C, and D permit reuse of a patient-contact mouthpiece between clients and conflict with this infection-control practice.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC guidance directly supports changing the spirometry mouthpiece and filter between patients to prevent reuse of contaminated patient-contact components.
candidate.source_document_title: A Rational Approach to Disinfection and Sterilization; Guidelines for Preventing Health-Care-Associated Pneumonia
candidate.source_locator: CDC 'A Rational Approach to Disinfection and Sterilization' → pulmonary-function equipment discussion: mouthpieces and spirometry tubing can become contaminated; filters may prevent distal equipment contamination; filters and proximal mouthpieces are changed between patients. CDC 'Guidelines for Preventing Health-Care-Associated Pneumonia' → Pulmonary-function testing equipment, recommendation 9.b: change the mouthpiece and filter of a spirometer between uses on different patients.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: CDC Infection Control guidance current and accessed 2026-08-18; pulmonary-function equipment recommendation retained on current CDC web resources
candidate.stem: A nurse assists with spirometry testing for several clients using the same spirometer. Which infection-prevention action is appropriate between clients?
